step_1_homogeneous_kelly.comment: uniform Kelly per event, no heterogeneity

step_3_hens_mayer_robust_lambda_2.rationale: λ=2 standard-error penalty zeros out bins where μ̂ < 2·SE.  Empirical retention based on real bin counts.

step_4_pyramid_fractioning.rationale: first leg full Kelly, pyramid legs /3; average ~70% across leg mix.

step_5_breadth_utilisation.rationale: position-blocking and pyramid fresh-pulse gate truncate the measurable BR.

step_6_cluster_independence.rationale: non-independence of trades within a Hawkes cluster reduces aggregate log-growth below sum of per-event terms.

math_verdict: The user's 80,000% target is unreachable under the actual E2E pipeline.  The homogeneous Kelly ceiling is ~5%/yr; heterogeneous (perfectly calibrated) is +83,779%/yr; but the cascade of REAL pipeline constraints — Hens-Mayer robust shrinkage, pyramid /N, breadth utilisation, cluster non-independence — collapses the achievable to ≈+6.0%/yr.  iter10 realises +26.1%/yr, aligning closely with the decomposition.  To unlock substantially higher returns would require a fundamentally NEW signal class — not aggressive sizing of the existing one (which the diagnostic shows is already at the noise floor).
